meta.title: Who originally recorded "Some Kind of Wonderful"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not Grand Funk Railroad. Soul Brothers Six cut it first, in 1967 on Atlantic, written by their own John Ellison. It stalled at No. 91.
meta.ogTitle: Who originally recorded 'Some Kind of Wonderful'?
meta.ogDescription: Grand Funk Railroad took it to No. 3 in 1975, but Soul Brothers Six recorded it first in 1967 on Atlantic. John Ellison wrote it and sang it.

answer.label: Not a Grand Funk Railroad original — a 1967 Soul Brothers Six single on Atlantic
answer.originalArtistDates: Active 1965-1976 · American R&B group from Rochester, New York
answer.sourceLine: Because Grand Funk Railroad’s thundering 1974 single is the version on classic-rock radio, the song is widely heard as a Grand Funk original. It is not. “(She’s) Some Kind of Wonderful” was written by John Ellison and first recorded by his own R&B group, Soul Brothers Six, at Atlantic Studios in New York City on March 30, 1967, issued that May as Atlantic 2406. That record reached only number 91 on the US Billboard Hot 100; Grand Funk’s Capitol single reached number three.

original.heading: Who recorded it first
original.label: Atlantic
original.released: Issued as a 7-inch single on Atlantic (Atlantic 2406) in May 1967, with “I’ll Be Loving You” on the B-side. It was recorded at Atlantic Studios in New York City on March 30, 1967.
original.charted: Number 91 on the US Billboard Hot 100 — a regional success, particularly in Philadelphia, that barely registered nationally.
original.cover: Grand Funk Railroad’s version, produced by Jimmy Ienner for the album All the Girls in the World Beware!!!, was released by Capitol (Capitol 4002) on December 9, 1974 and reached number three on the US Billboard Hot 100 on February 22, 1975.

trail: Wikipedia’s article on the song gives the recording date, studio, label and catalogue number, and states plainly that it was first recorded by Soul Brothers Six in 1967 ↗, with Grand Funk’s 1974 reading described as the best-known version.
MusicBrainz holds a recording entity for the Soul Brothers Six performance ↗ whose earliest release is the May 1967 US single “Some Kind of Wonderful / I’ll Be Loving You.”
The songwriter’s own biography ↗ places him in Soul Brothers Six as lead guitarist, singer and writer, composing the song on the way to a 1967 session.
Grand Funk’s single is documented on the same page with its Capitol catalogue number, its December 9, 1974 release date and its number-three peak on February 22, 1975 ↗.

authors.name: Soul Brothers Six
authors.heading: Soul Brothers Six
authors.metaLine: American R&B group, Rochester, New York · active 1965-1976
authors.bio: Soul Brothers Six formed in Rochester, New York in the mid-1960s around the five Armstrong brothers — Sam, Charles, Moses, Harry and Gene — who performed as the Soul Brothers Five until West Virginia-born singer and guitarist John Ellison joined and made them six. They cut “Some Kind of Wonderful” for Atlantic at the label’s New York studio on March 30, 1967; it was released that May backed with “I’ll Be Loving You.” The A-side scraped the Hot 100 at number 91 and the group broke up in the 1970s, but the B-side became a fixture of the British Northern soul scene. Their record, not Grand Funk’s, is the first one.

authors.name: Grand Funk Railroad
authors.heading: Grand Funk Railroad
authors.bio: Grand Funk Railroad recorded the song for their 1974 album All the Girls in the World Beware!!!, with Jimmy Ienner producing. Capitol issued it as a single (Capitol 4002) on December 9, 1974, and it reached number three on the US Billboard Hot 100 on February 22, 1975 — strong enough to place sixth on Billboard’s year-end Hot 100 for 1975. It is a superb, thoroughly earned hit; the only error is chronological, since the band did not originate the song and never claimed to have written it.

authors.name: John Ellison
authors.heading: John Ellison
authors.metaLine: b. August 11, 1941, Montgomery, West Virginia · singer, guitarist and songwriter
authors.bio: Willie John Ellison was born in Montgomery, West Virginia in 1941 and raised in the coalfield community of Landgraff before moving to Rochester, New York, where he joined Soul Brothers Six as lead guitarist, singer and writer. He wrote “(She’s) Some Kind of Wonderful” quickly while travelling to a 1967 recording session, and it went on to be recorded by dozens of other artists; BMI cited it in 1995 as one of the most-performed songs in its catalogue. Ellison took Canadian citizenship in 2006 and was inducted into the West Virginia Music Hall of Fame in 2015 and the Rochester Music Hall of Fame in 2024.

misattribution.heading: Right song, wrong originator
misattribution.intro: The song is routinely filed as a Grand Funk Railroad original. It is a cover of a soul single that came out on Atlantic in 1967.

items.why: Their Capitol single, released December 9, 1974, reached number three on the US Billboard Hot 100 on February 22, 1975 and has stayed on rock radio ever since. It is a cover.
Recorded at Atlantic Studios in New York City on March 30, 1967 and released that May as Atlantic 2406, backed with “I’ll Be Loving You.” It peaked at number 91.
Ellison wrote it and sang lead on the original as a member of Soul Brothers Six. He is credited on every version, including Grand Funk’s.

misattribution.truthLine: First recorded by Soul Brothers Six, Atlantic 2406, May 1967 — written by their own John Ellison.

context.heading: Why the cover swallowed the original
lead: The interesting question is not who wrote it — John Ellison’s name is on every label, including Grand Funk’s. It is why a 1967 Atlantic soul 45 by the song’s own author sank at number 91 while a 1974 rock reading of the same tune went to number three. Part of the answer is format: Soul Brothers Six were an R&B group on a label crowded with bigger R&B names, and their single got regional traction without national push. Ellison has said he believed the record was held back by racial prejudice in radio programming of the era.

The other part is that Grand Funk’s version arrived at the exact moment the band was at its commercial peak, with Jimmy Ienner producing them for a mass pop audience. Once a song lands on classic-rock radio and stays there for decades, the earlier record has to compete with a memory. The original is not obscure — it sits on Atlantic soul compilations and was praised by critic Dave Marsh — but it is outnumbered.
detailsBody: March 30, 1967 — Soul Brothers Six record “Some Kind of Wonderful,” written by their own John Ellison, at Atlantic Studios in New York City.
May 1967 — Atlantic issues the single as Atlantic 2406, backed with “I’ll Be Loving You.” It peaks at number 91 on the US Billboard Hot 100.
1968 — The Fantastic Johnny C covers it and reaches number 87 on the Hot 100, just missing where the original landed.
1974 — Grand Funk Railroad cut it for All the Girls in the World Beware!!!; Capitol releases the single on December 9, 1974.
February 22, 1975 — The Grand Funk single peaks at number three, and finishes sixth on Billboard’s year-end Hot 100 for 1975.
Later covers include The Fantastic Johnny C, Huey Lewis and the News (number 44 in 1994) and Toploader (number 76 in the UK, 2002).
context.pull: The writer sang it first, and still lost the song to a cover.
